semantic_findings: SandboxExecutor provides timeout, virtual-memory/process-count ulimits, process-group kill and temporary working-directory cleanup, but these are resource controls rather than an isolation boundary.
The allow_network configuration flag is stored but never enforced; allow_network=false does not disable network access.
Child processes inherit os.environ, so credentials/tokens/configuration present in the parent environment can be visible to executed code unless separately stripped upstream.
No filesystem namespace/chroot/container/seccomp/capability boundary is established; code can address normal user-visible filesystem paths despite running from a temporary cwd.
bash and sh are first-class interpreters, so arbitrary shell effects remain possible under the parent user's permissions.
The rust path runs rustc on the source but does not execute the resulting binary, violating the executor's language-neutral execute contract.

dedup.overlap: Historical Genesis sandbox archaeology already established that timeout/output/resource controls alone are not a security sandbox.
new_writer_specific_oracles: configuration-flag enforcement: allow_network=false must have an observable network-deny effect
filesystem isolation/effect mediation rather than temp-cwd semantics
compile-success must not be reported as execution-success for compiled languages

target_law: Safe-Effect/Clay authority must mediate effects even inside a code execution sandbox; a sandbox label never grants authority.
Sandbox configuration must be fail-closed and testable: declared network/filesystem/process restrictions must correspond to enforced runtime behavior.
Execution receipts must distinguish compile, launch, runtime result, timeout/cancel and effect-denial phases.
